$comment: ZERO vetted catalog of EXTERNAL MCP servers. Data only — ZERO never installs or launches these itself. Versions are pinned; re-verify before bumping. Secrets are referenced as ${VAR} and are expanded by Claude Code from YOUR environment — never write values here.

entries.name: Playwright MCP (Microsoft)
entries.purpose: Drive a real browser via accessibility snapshots: navigate, click, fill forms, screenshots, e2e checks of web apps.
entries.reason: Official, Apache-2.0, very active (push 2026-11-03, 1 open issue), no API keys, runs locally. Hardening flags exist (--isolated, --allowed-origins, --sandbox).
requires: downloads a browser on first use (~150MB)
risks: The browser can reach any site unless --allowed-origins is set
Pages are untrusted input (prompt injection via page text)

entries.name: Chrome DevTools MCP (Google)
entries.purpose: Performance traces, network/console inspection, Lighthouse-style debugging in Chrome.
entries.reason: Strong for perf debugging, but usage statistics are collected BY DEFAULT and performance tools may send trace URLs to Google CrUX. Both are disabled below.
requires: Google Chrome or Chrome for Testing
risks: Overlaps with Playwright MCP — enable one browser server at a time to save context

entries.name: GitHub MCP Server (official, remote)
entries.purpose: Issues, PRs, code, Actions, security alerts via the official GitHub API.
entries.reason: Official, MIT, active. Supports read-only mode, toolset filtering and lockdown via headers — exactly the least-privilege controls ZERO wants.

secrets.name: GITHUB_PAT
secrets.purpose: Fine-grained PAT. Start read-only: Contents/Issues/Pull requests = Read. Scope it to the repos you need.

risks: A write-scoped PAT lets the agent push/merge
hardening: X-MCP-Readonly: true until you need writes
fine-grained PAT limited to specific repos

entries.name: Context7 (Upstash)
entries.purpose: Up-to-date, version-specific library documentation injected on demand (fights outdated API knowledge).
entries.reason: Very useful and free tier works without a key, but it is a hosted service: library names and your queries leave the machine.
entries.cost: free tier; API key recommended for higher limits
risks: Queries sent to a third party — do not paste proprietary code into queries

entries.name: Knowledge Graph Memory (reference server)
entries.purpose: Local entity/relation/observation graph stored in one JSONL file.
entries.reason: Official, tiny (2 deps), fully local. But Claude Code already has CLAUDE.md + subagent `memory` scopes; use this only for cross-project facts that don't belong in a repo.
risks: Memory can accumulate personal data — review the JSONL file periodically
hardening: Keep MEMORY_FILE_PATH outside any git repo

entries.name: DBHub (Bytebase)
entries.purpose: Postgres/MySQL/SQL Server/SQLite/MariaDB access with read-only mode, row limits and query timeouts.
entries.reason: Token-conscious, MIT, active, guardrails built in. Enable per project when a database exists.

secrets.name: ZERO_DB_DSN
secrets.purpose: Connection string — use a READ-ONLY database user

risks: DSN contains a password — keep it in env, never in .mcp.json values
hardening: Enable DBHub read-only mode in its TOML config

entries.name: Serena (semantic code tools via LSP)
entries.purpose: Symbol-level navigation and editing (find references, rename) for large codebases.
entries.reason: Powerful for >100k LOC repos, but Python + language servers add weight; application is GPL-3.0-or-later (fine as a separate process, do not copy code). Current projects are small enough for Grep/Glob.

entries.name: Brave Search MCP
entries.reason: Claude Code already ships WebSearch/WebFetch. Worth it only if you need a second index or image/news verticals. Requires API key.

entries.name: Firecrawl MCP
entries.purpose: Crawl/scrape whole sites into clean markdown, structured extraction.
entries.reason: Best-in-class crawling, but paid hosted API. Built-in WebFetch covers single pages.

entries.name: Fetch (reference server, Python)
entries.purpose: Fetch a URL and convert to markdown.
entries.reason: Redundant with Claude Code's built-in WebFetch. NOTE: the npm package named `mcp-server-fetch` is a security placeholder (0.0.1-security) for removed malware — the real one is the PyPI package.
hardening: Keep default private-IP guard (do not pass --allow-private-ips)

entries.name: Filesystem (reference server)
entries.reason: Redundant inside Claude Code (native Read/Edit/Write/Glob/Grep with permission rules). Useful only for Claude Desktop.
risks: Duplicates native tools, doubles the context cost

entries.name: Sequential Thinking (reference server)
entries.reason: Current Claude models reason natively (extended thinking); the tool adds context cost without new capability.
